<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Seven people are dead and 14 others injured after a [[Boko Haram]] [[suicide bombing|suicide bomber]] blew himself up at a village hosting internally displaced people in [[Far North Region, Cameroon|Far North]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-security-bokoharam-cameroun/seven-killed-in-suicide-bomb-attack-in-northern-cameroon-village-idUSKBN25T30O (''Reuters'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[List of changes made due to the George Floyd protests|Changes made due to the George Floyd protests]]
**The [[BBC]] reverses its controversial decision to ban the songs "[[Rule, Britannia!]]" and "[[Land of Hope and Glory]]" from the 2020 [[The Proms|Last Night of the Proms]] over concerns over their links to [[colonialism]] and slavery. Critics of the songs, including [[Chi-chi Nwanoku]] and [[Gareth Malone]], say the songs are "outdated" and glorify racism. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-53998584 (BBC News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***The [[Economy of Australia|economy]] officially enters a [[recession]] for the first time since [[1991 in Australia|1991]] after the [[Australian Bureau of Statistics|Bureau of Statistics]] reports a 7% decline in [[Gross domestic product|GDP]] over the second quarter, the largest fall since records began in 1959. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-australia-officially-in-recession-gdp-june-quarter-fall/527626f3-7357-48a1-901d-5d942c47d82a (9 News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Tropical Storm Nana (2020)|Tropical Storm Nana]] is expected to strengthen into a strong tropical storm before it makes landfall in [[Belize]] tomorrow. [https://www.sun-sentinel.com/news/weather/hurricane/fl-ne-hurricane-nana-tropical-storms-20200902-a7qb7bekxjamhk2xffxbdo334i-story.html (''The Sun-Sentinel'')]
**[[Hurricane force wind warning|Hurricane warnings]] are issued on Belize's coast in case hurricane-force winds are present. [https://weather.com/storms/hurricane/news/2020-09-01-tropical-storm-nana-caribbean-forecast (The Weather Channel)]
*[[MV Wakashio oil spill|MV ''Wakashio'' oil spill]]
**[[Mauritius]] asks [[Japan]] to pay [[United States dollar|$]]34 million in reparations for the disaster and demands the money to "support local fishermen whose livelihoods were adversely impacted by an oil leak last month", according to a [[Mauritian government]] document. [https://www.dw.com/en/mauritius-asks-japan-to-pay-34-million-after-oil-spill-report/a-54789180 (DW)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota]]
****[[Bloomington, Minnesota|Bloomington]]-based [[HealthPartners]] announces that they are seeking 1,500 patients for the [[Phases of clinical research#Phase III|phase 3 trials]] for [[AstraZeneca]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.startribune.com/minnesotans-sought-for-virus-vaccine-trial-by-healthpartners/572294742/ (''The Star-Tribune'')]
****[[Minnesota]] reports the first death tied to the [[Sturgis Motorcycle Rally]] in [[South Dakota]], which drew hundreds of thousands of bikers despite COVID-19 concerns. The patient was a male biker in his 60s. At least 50 cases in Minnesota have been linked to Sturgis. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/sturgis-motorcycle-rally-covid-19-death-minnesota/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iowa]]
****[[Cedar Rapids, Iowa|Cedar Rapids]] mayor [[Brad Hart]] issues a [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for the city as [[Iowa]] becomes one of the leading states in rising COVID-19 cases. [https://www.thegazette.com/subject/news/cedar-rapids-mask-mandate-iowa-coronavirus-masks-required-covid-19-20200902 (''The Cedar Rapids Gazette'')]
***The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] requests [[State governments of the United States|state governments]] for their assistance to dispatch an unspecified, potential COVID-19 vaccine to local wholesalers by November 1. [https://www.philstar.com/world/2020/09/03/2039816/us-states-told-be-ready-distribute-covid-19-vaccine-november-1 (AFP via ''The Philippine Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****Greece reports the first case in its largest [[refugee camp]], located on the island of [[Lesbos]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2020/09/02/first-coronavirus-case-in-greeces-main-migrant-camp/ (AFP via ''Manila Bulletin'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****Former [[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Silvio Berlusconi]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. He is expected to self-isolate at his home near [[Milan]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/silvio-berlusconi-former-italy-pm-tests-positive-for-coronavirus-12061938 (Sky News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] registers its highest number of new cases since April 1, with 55 new cases reported in the last 24 hours. [https://www.rtvslo.si/zdravje/novi-koronavirus/tretji-najvisji-dnevni-prirast-okuzb-doslej-v-torek-potrjenih-55-primerov/534919 (RTVSLO)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 1,508 cases, an increase from 1,295 yesterday. Some lockdowns are [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|re-imposed]] in [[Greater Manchester]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/live/2020/sep/02/uk-coronavirus-live-local-lockdowns-boris-johnson-pmqs (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|government]] considers providing free COVID-19 vaccines for all citizens. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-japan-vaccine-idUSKBN25T09L (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
****The number of cases in [[Kyrgyzstan]] reaches past 44,000. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-09/02/c_139337572.htm (Xinhuanet)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] marks 100 days without new COVID-19 cases. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/514754-thailand-goes-100-days-without-locally-transmitted-covid-19-case (''The Hill'')]

;International relations
*[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Maldives]]
***The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Maldives)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] tightens [[Visa policy of Maldives|the country's visa policy]] for [[Tourism in the Maldives|tourists]], requiring all tourists to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|test result]], after it was reported that at least 45 people at several of [[:Category:Resorts in the Maldives|the country's resorts]] have contracted the virus. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/maldives-tightens-tourist-virus-rules-spike-covid-19-cases-13075610 (CNA)]
**The [[Taiwan]]ese [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Taiwan)|foreign ministry]] unveils a new design to [[Taiwan passport|the country's passport]] cover after claiming that the current design has led foreign governments into mistakenly imposing COVID-19 pandemic-related travel restrictions intended for [[Chinese nationality law|mainland Chinese citizens]] on [[Taiwanese nationality law|Taiwanese citizens]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/taiwan-redesigns-passport-to-avoid-confusion-with-china/a-54789718 (DW)]
*[[2020 China–India skirmishes]], [[Internet censorship in India]]
**India bans 118 apps linked to Chinese companies including popular [[Tencent]]-backed video game ''[[PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds#Mobile versions|PUBG Mobile]]'', stating they are "prejudicial to sovereignty and integrity of India". [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-02/tencent-s-pubg-banned-by-india-as-tensions-with-china-escalate (Bloomberg)]
*[[China–United States relations]]
**[[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces new restrictions on [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China|senior Chinese diplomats]] visiting the U.S., requiring them to secure an approval from U.S. authorities to meet with [[Local government in the United States|local government]] officials or to visit [[Higher education in the United States|universities and colleges in the country]]. Pompeo describes the restrictions as a "[[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocal move]]" after the [[Chinese government]] had imposed similar restrictions on U.S. officials. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20200903/p2g/00m/0in/056000c (Kyodo News via ''The Mainichi'')]
*[[Saudi Arabia–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] opens its [[airspace]] to all flights between the [[United Arab Emirates]] and "all countries", upon the request of the [[government of the United Arab Emirates|Emirati government]]. The move comes days after [[Israel]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] restored diplomatic ties and Israeli [[flag carrier]] [[El Al]] commenced commercial flights to the UAE. [[Saudi Arabia]] still maintains a policy of neither maintaining  diplomatic ties nor [[International recognition of Israel|recognising Israel]], and does not allow Israeli aircraft to fly in Saudi Arabian airspace under any other circumstances. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/saudi-allows-overflights-by-uae-services-to--all-countries--13076270 (AFP via CNA)]
*The [[United States]] places sanctions on several senior officials in the [[International Criminal Court]], including [[Prosecutor of the International Criminal Court|Chief Prosecutor]] [[Fatou Bensouda]], for launching an investigation into [[International Criminal Court investigation in Afghanistan|allegations of American war crimes]] in the [[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|current Afghanistan war]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-54003527 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital punishment in Saudi Arabia]], aftermath of the [[2014 al-Dalwah attack]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] sentences seven [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] militants [[capital punishment|to death]] over a 2014 [[mass shooting]] that killed eight [[Shia Islam in Saudi Arabia|Shiite]] Muslims near the city of [[Hofuf|al-Ahsa]]. Three other convicts were given 25-year jail sentences. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-saudi-security/saudi-arabia-sentences-seven-islamist-militants-to-death-over-killings-of-shiites-idUSKBN25T1WO?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[Charlie Hebdo shooting|''Charlie Hebdo'' shooting]]
**Fourteen people are on trial in [[France]] for their involvement in the [[Charlie Hebdo shooting|2015 attack]] on the satirical magazine ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]''. Three are being [[Trial in absentia|tried ''in absentia'']]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53975350 (BBC News)]
*[[Global surveillance disclosures (2013–present)]]
**The [[U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit]] rules that the [[global surveillance]] programs of the [[National Security Agency]] disclosed by former [[Central Intelligence Agency]] employee [[Edward Snowden]] in 2013 are unconstitutional, having violated the [[Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6908201/spy-program-exposed-by-snowden-illegal/?cs=14264 (AAP via ''The Canberra Times'')] [https://www.dw.com/en/nsa-snowden/a-54797779 (DW)]
*Eight people are killed and 14 others injured after gunmen [[mass shooting|open fire]] on a group of people gathered to mourn the death of a youth who was killed in a motorcycle accident in [[Cuernavaca]], [[Morelos]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-54013217 (BBC News)]
*[[Kang Kek Iew]] (better known as ''Comrade Duch''), former [[Khmer Rouge]] leader and convicted [[war criminal]], dies in a [[Phnom Penh]] hospital at age 77. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/01/world/asia/duch-kaing-guek-eav-dead.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Zimbabwe]]an journalist [[Hopewell Chin'ono]] is granted [[bail]] after being arrested for more than a month on charges of [[Incitement|inciting]] public violence over [[Twitter|tweeting]] in support of anti-[[government of Zimbabwe|government]] protests. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/09/02/zimbabwean-journalist-hopewell-chinono-granted-bail-held-jail/ (''The Telegraph'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**The [[German government]] reports it has "unequivocal evidence" to confirm the poisoning of Russian opposition figure [[Alexei Navalny]] by a [[Novichok agent]], according to tests conducted by a ''[[Bundeswehr]]''-run laboratory. [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] calls Navalny "a victim of attempted murder". [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/09/02/germany-says-russian-dissident-navalny-without-a-doubt-poisoned-by-novichok-nerve-agent.html (CNBC)] [https://www.npr.org/2020/09/02/908753772/alexei-navalny-was-poisoned-with-novichok-nerve-agent-germany-says (NPR)]
*The ''[[Royal Thai Government Gazette]]'' reports that [[Monarchy of Thailand|Thai King]] [[Vajiralongkorn]] restored the rank and titles of former royal consort [[Sineenat Bilaskalayani]]. Her titles were stripped last October after the court accused her of disobedience and trying to raise herself to "the same state as the queen". [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-53994198 (BBC News)]
